title: AEOeye vs Trakkr: Free Instant Audit or Daily Paid Monitoring?
metaTitle: AEOeye vs Trakkr: Honest AI Visibility Comparison
metaDescription: AEOeye vs Trakkr compared honestly: free instant AI visibility audit vs daily paid monitoring across 8 models. See pricing, engines, speed and who each fits.
shortAnswer: AEOeye gives a free, instant AI visibility audit — no signup or trial clock — so a non-expert sees in seconds whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini recommend their brand. Trakkr is a trial-then-paid platform ($79+/mo) built for ongoing, daily monitoring across 8 AI models with competitor benchmarking, citation mapping and weekly action playbooks. Choose AEOeye to check fast and free; choose Trakkr if you have a team to run continuous, agency-grade tracking.
intro:
AEOeye and Trakkr both answer the same question — are AI models recommending your brand? — but they're built for different moments. AEOeye is a free, instant audit you run before committing to anything. Trakkr is a subscription that watches your AI visibility every day and gives your team a workflow to act on it.

This is a fair head-to-head. Trakkr is genuinely strong at ongoing monitoring and is built for agencies and marketing teams; AEOeye is newer and lighter on enterprise analytics and historical dashboards. The right pick depends on whether you need a quick answer or a continuous program.

sections.heading: The core difference: a free check vs. a paid program
sections.body:
The cleanest way to separate these two is by commitment. AEOeye is a free, instant audit. You enter your brand and a buyer-style question, and within seconds you see whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini recommend you, roughly where you rank, and which competitors are winning the answer. No card, no trial clock, no sales call — it's designed so a non-expert gets a clear read in one sitting.

Trakkr is a program, not a one-off check. After a 14-day free trial (no card), it becomes a recurring subscription starting at $79/mo that tracks your visibility daily across eight AI models and assembles trends, benchmarks and playbooks over time. That ongoing cadence is the point — and the cost.

So the decision isn't really 'which tool is better.' It's whether you need to *find out now* (AEOeye) or *watch continuously and act every week* (Trakkr). Many teams start with a free AEOeye audit to see if there's a problem worth a paid monitoring subscription at all.

sections.heading: Where Trakkr is genuinely stronger
sections.body:
Credit where it's due: for ongoing, multi-brand monitoring, Trakkr does more than a free audit can. It tracks eight AI models — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Grok, DeepSeek and Meta AI — on a daily basis, so you see trends rather than a single snapshot. It adds competitor benchmarking, citation source mapping (which pages and domains the models pull from), perception scoring, and weekly prioritized action playbooks that tell your team what to fix next.

It's also built for agencies. The Scale plan ($399/mo) covers 10 brands with white-label reporting and API access — useful if AI visibility is a service you sell to clients. AEOeye, by contrast, is lighter on historical dashboards and enterprise-grade analytics today; its deeper multi-engine querying activates with usage rather than arriving as a polished daily command center on day one.

If you have marketing capacity to run a continuous AEO/GEO program and want one dashboard to manage it, Trakkr is built for exactly that, and it's a reasonable choice.

sections.heading: Where AEOeye wins: speed, price and zero friction
sections.body:
AEOeye's edge is that there's nothing to commit to. It's free to start, instant, and requires no signup, no card and no contract — which matters most for the people Trakkr's pricing pinches: solo founders, small businesses and anyone who just wants to know where they stand before spending.

Three practical advantages stand out. First, time-to-answer: AEOeye returns a result in seconds, versus setting up prompts and waiting for daily data to accumulate. Second, the learning curve: AEOeye is built for non-experts, so you don't need acquired intuition about AI behavior to read it — a common complaint about dashboards is that they show data but not always what to do. Third, blind multi-engine querying: it asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini the questions real buyers ask, so the result reflects genuine recommendations, not a self-flattering setup.

The honest trade-off: AEOeye is lighter on long-run trend history and the agency tooling Trakkr offers. If continuous tracking is your job, you'll eventually want more than a free audit gives.

sections.heading: Cost and the small-business question
sections.body:
Cost is where the two diverge most. AEOeye's core audit is free, so the barrier to a first answer is zero. Trakkr offers a 14-day trial with no card, but there's no open free tier for ongoing use — to keep monitoring you commit to a recurring subscription. Reviews repeatedly note it 'may be steep for small businesses,' and that fuller value sits in the higher Scale tier (~$399/mo). Annual billing saves roughly 17%.

There are real constraints to plan around on Trakkr regardless of price. Tracking is capped at 50 prompts per brand even on paid plans, which can feel tight as you broaden coverage. And because AI answers vary across models and shift over time, Trakkr is explicitly a trend-tracking tool, not an exact ranking — the whole AEO category is young and best practices keep moving.

The sensible path for budget-conscious teams: run AEOeye free first. If it surfaces a clear, recurring visibility gap and you have the capacity to act on weekly playbooks, Trakkr's subscription may pay for itself. If you mainly need to check and occasionally re-check, the free audit is enough.

keyTakeaways: AEOeye is a free, instant AI visibility audit — no signup, card or trial clock; Trakkr is a trial-then-paid subscription starting at $79/mo.
Trakkr is genuinely stronger for ongoing work: daily tracking across 8 AI models, competitor benchmarking, citation mapping, perception scoring and weekly action playbooks.
Trakkr is built for agencies and marketing teams — the $399/mo Scale plan adds 10 brands, white-label reporting and API access.
AEOeye wins on speed (seconds to first result), price (free), and ease for non-experts who don't want to read dashboards.
Honest limits: AEOeye is lighter on historical dashboards and enterprise analytics; Trakkr caps tracking at 50 prompts per brand and gives data, not done-for-you fixes.
Smart move: run AEOeye free first to see if there's a problem, then commit to Trakkr if you have the team to run continuous monitoring.

faqs.q: Is AEOeye really free, or is it a trial like Trakkr?
faqs.a: AEOeye's core audit is genuinely free to run — no card, no signup requirement and no trial countdown. Trakkr offers a 14-day free trial (no card), but after that it's a paid subscription starting at $79/mo, with no open free tier for ongoing use.

faqs.q: How many AI engines does each tool check?
faqs.a: AEOeye queries ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini with the questions real buyers ask. Trakkr tracks eight models daily: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Grok, DeepSeek and Meta AI. Trakkr covers more engines and tracks them continuously over time.

faqs.q: Which is better for a small business or solo founder?
faqs.a: Usually AEOeye to start. It's free and instant, so you can see where you stand without committing budget. Trakkr is powerful but reviews note its subscription 'may be steep for small businesses,' and the fuller value sits in the $399/mo Scale tier. If you later need daily monitoring and have time to act on it, Trakkr makes sense.

faqs.q: Does Trakkr fix my AI visibility automatically?
faqs.a: No. Trakkr provides data, benchmarks and prioritized playbooks, but reviews stress it shows what's happening, not always why, and it doesn't make the fixes for you. You need some marketing capacity and intuition about AI behavior to turn its dashboards into results.

Yes, and it's a reasonable approach. Use AEOeye's free audit to quickly check or re-check whether AI models recommend you, and use Trakkr if you want a continuous, agency-grade program with daily tracking, competitor benchmarking and weekly action plans.
